subject: Biotechnology
title: Marker-Assisted Selection
description: A quick win: understand Marker-Assisted Selection.

hook.text: You cannot see drought tolerance by looking at a seedling — but DNA markers reveal it in hours.

buildup.text: MAS links physical traits to DNA sequences — breeders screen seedlings with molecular tests, not field trials.

discovery.text: Thousands of seedlings are tested at once — only those carrying the desired markers advance to the field.

twist.text: MAS is not genetic modification — no foreign DNA is added. It speeds up conventional breeding with molecular tools.

climax.text: Flood-tolerant rice Sub1 was developed using MAS — saving millions of tons of rice in monsoon regions.

punchline.text: Read DNA, pick the best seeds — molecular markers accelerate breeding.

quiz.question: Why is marker-assisted selection not considered genetic modification?
options: It uses chemicals instead of DNA technology
It selects plants based on natural DNA markers without inserting foreign genes
It only works on wild plants, not cultivated crops
